If what we are looking for is a quality leap with lighter colors and shades and a look very similar to the pine or spruce wood flooring, the Pure Bamboo range will delight all our guests or guests. Its normal or roasted format offers us the possibility to choose between two totally different styles to decorate our space. With the models of a reputed flooring brand Bamboo range, they have at our disposal all the possibilities of choice. With this solid bamboo flooring you will achieve the perfect natural finish you were looking for in your rooms and feel a sense of warmth every time you step on the floor of your home.

item.title: Bamboo Veneers - The solid choice for solid housing
item.source: Bamboo Veneers - The solid choice for solid housing
item.description:
Bamboo is a solid choice when it comes to decorating the floors of our home according to sustainability because they are the fastest growing known ground plants, up to one meter in 24 hours. There are several types that adapt to the different needs of each room, since it is not the same room for children as the kitchen or the living room. 

Resistance and color vary in the different modalities of bamboo. If there is an environmental condition where the use of bamboo is not recommended, it is excessive moisture or too much environmental dryness, which is not different from most woods.

When it comes to an area of the house that receives a lot of people, it is advisable to lean over the woven strand bamboo as it is more resistant and durable. 

In any case, the quality of bamboo is determined by its age. Between 5.5 and 6 years of growth is the ideal time to ensure a mature, solid and durable fiber. Still, bamboo is not considered hardwood, compared to that of trees with longer ripening cycles. Meanwhile, bamboo grows like a weed and hence is considered more sustainable.

For their manufacture, the bamboo pieces are glued together by face or edge, according to whether vertical or horizontal streaks of bamboo are required, forming blocks by hot pressing, which once softened by immersion in water, are cut into sheets. Said plates are dried to the correct moisture content and then sanded and profiled for sewing.

Bamboo veneer and bamboo skin veneers are getting more and more attention in the construction in today‘s society. These bamboo products are mainly used for wall, floor, roof decoration and indoor and outdoor building decorations, with a lot of features. Bamboo Woven Veneers and Bamboo Skin has the characteristics of natural texture, simple and natural, and advanced surface wear resistance, which has been widely used in practice and obtain suppressive power in desired results.

Bamboo Woven Veneers appears to provide a new high flavor to the decoration of the house and the choice to equalize. Bamboo furniture in the bamboo furniture manufacturing industry and new interior decoration industry, as new natural environmental protection material, can be widely used, it has wide possibilities. Bamboo Knitting is a type of pure handmade decorative material for furniture and interior decoration.

Bamboo veneer in the form of bamboo panels but providing the same color and grains at significant low cost!

The bamboo veneer is cut from the pressed bamboo block. It provides the same color and grains as the bamboo panels. This can be applied to plywood veneering, indoor decoration, engineered flooring etc. to avoid cracks during combat, the bamboo veneer enables easy to press the veneer sheet on a panel, which is a thin cellulose wool or paper thin, but with stronger support.

Production process for product- Stip (strips can be added in 5 different ways :)

1. Plain pressed- Bamboo strips are pressed against each other horizontally and sticking under high pressure, specialty bamboo nodes are clearly visible

2. Side pressed- Bamboo strips are pressed against each other and sticking under high pressure, specialty bamboo nodes are not very pronounced

3. Weaving thread- Strips are connected through thread weaving, as well as, a fabric support product is applied to make it more rigid, this is the base material for carpet / tile products.

4. Tape- Strips are connected through placing tape on reverse. In addition, a fabric support product is applied to make it more rigid, it can also be used as the base material for carpet / tile products.

5. Density- This one is made in a different way, bamboo strips are crushed and pressed together with ultra-high pressure, in this process a very durable end product that is equal to the hardness of a wood completely change the structure.

Keep the above mentioned things in mind when you are going to buy Bamboo veneers. The wrong choice of product not only will cost you double but also create an imperfect look at your home. Use expert advice in case you are unsure of your choice.

item.title: Stranded Woven Bamboo Flooring- why go for it?
item.source: Stranded Woven Bamboo Flooring- why go for it?
item.description:
Strand woven bamboo flooring is one of the most popular options when it comes to flooring on the market right now. It is a specialized kind of bamboo floor that has certain benefits over the regular ones. What differentiates this type of bamboo flooring from other ones is its hardness that can be further increased via the lamination process. While the bamboo floors are quite eco friendly and popular, as the process used for hardening used takes away the most significant and troublesome characteristics, as per the installers. 


Hardness


Hardness is a big factor and concern when it comes to bamboo flooring. While it is that bamboo flooring is durable and affordable when compared to other products, it is incapable of taking up the abuses that hardwood flooring is famous to endure. In order to make it more suitable covering option for your floor, stranded woven bamboo floors are further altered using glue to help bonding different strips together once they have been boiled in order to eliminate any sugar residues, as sugar is known to attract termites that can create problem in future. 


Carbonized Bamboo


Amongst the most popular products is the carbonized bamboo! This is the bamboo is put up through the boiling process that makes it darker as compared to the natural bamboo flooring. However, the boiling process tends to make the wood even softer. The stranded woven bamboo flooring available in the market offers alternative that provide it with rich color associated with the carbonized bamboo. It creates much harder planks with better characteristics. As compared to the hardwood floors, bamboo is likely to match it in hardness. In terms of care, with bamboo products in the form of stranded woven products, you can get study durable floors that provide years of longevity. 


The Universal Benefits


Strand woven bamboo also offers some exceptional benefits as compared to natural bamboo flooring. It is easier to keep this flooring into good shape. It can easily withstand heels, hard sole shoes and other form of traffic and abuses on visits throughout the day. When the planks become dirtier, you can clean it up easily with the help of a damp cloth or you can also use elbow grease. There is no need of using harsh cleansers on stranded woven bamboo as you need with the hardwood floors. 


You must be able to get warranty period on your bamboo woven flooring. You must check to see how long your manufacturers are ready to backup the product and provide protection against. You must keep in mind right from the start that the bamboo flooring is never the right choice for areas when people enter the house or other section where in it tends to face traffic with people wearing hard soles and boots. 


However, in a living room, you can try installing stranded woven bamboo floors or other commercialized flooring options. Strand woven bamboo flooring can sometimes be laid right over the top of your existing floor, so be sure to ask if this is an option for your home.


Strand woven bamboo flooring has very unique design and the density is much higher than normal floor, it is 1, 250 kg/m3, so it is really strong and it is not so easy to bend or cramp.


1. Color symmetry because the bamboo growth year is much shorter than the trees, so the sun is not seriously affected that no significant difference between the sun and the shadow side, so the bamboo floors are rich in bamboo grain and color symmetry;


2. Another brilliant benefit of bamboo flooring is the high surface hardness. For ex. the bamboo plant belongs to the lawn with plant fiber structure is its hardness is, of course, more than double the wood, no deformation.


3. Lifetime, Theoretically bamboo flooring life of up to 20 years. Compared, genuine wood, bamboo flooring has smaller contraction and extension, and keep their stability.


4. Keep warm, due to its large specific heat and its high density, so bamboo flooring in winter heat cannot loss, therefore, bamboo flooring has function of keeping warm.

item.title: Things to See When You Buy Solid Bamboo Flooring for Your Basement
item.source: Things to See When You Buy Solid Bamboo Flooring for Your Basement
item.description:
Bamboo floors look very different from traditional wood. When choosing a floor made of bamboo, also consider the environmental implications of a bamboo harvest.


Source


Bamboo flooring is often chosen because it is considered "greener" than other wood products. While oak, pine, and other trees require decades to regenerate after harvesting, bamboo is one of the fastest growing plants on the planet. However, there is very little regulation of bamboo harvests, which can affect wildlife and local ecosystems.


Effects on health


Many bamboo wood floors, among them, are mounted using adhesives containing volatile organic compounds (VOCs). These substances release toxic gases through a process known as "gas evolution," which can last several years after installation. VOCs are believed to cause respiratory problems, especially in children or the elderly. Choose bamboo floors labeled "VOC free" to avoid these compounds.


Characteristics


Bamboo floors are constructed in two basic shapes, each providing a very different appearance. Traditional bamboo is cut into long strips and glued to a wooden plank. This material is softer than most hardwoods and has a "striped" appearance that shows the bamboo strips. The stranded bamboo fabric is made by shredding the wood, then mixed with resin or adhesive. This mixture is pressed to form large pieces of wood and then sliced to create hardwood floors. Bamboo woven strand has a wood grain similar to traditional timber.


Installation


Homeowners can choose between two basic techniques when installing solid bamboo flooring. Some varieties are designed to be nailed or glued to the subsoil. These bamboo floors are made to look like traditional wood floors. Other varieties are floated on the subsoil, using a system of tongue and groove connectors. Floating floors are considered a better option for those planning a do-it-yourself project.


End up


Depending on the source of the bamboo plants, soils derived from them may have a natural beech finish or a darker brown shade. Some solid bamboo flooring are available with colorants or integral pigments to create colors that are not found in nature. When choosing bamboo floors, pay particular attention to whether the finish is vertical or horizontal. Vertical bamboo floors have a relatively uniform appearance, with stripes at regular intervals. Horizontal tiles are designed to show the unique qualities of bamboo and may have a visible discoloration and patterns some homeowners do not like.



Basement and bamboo floor


Install the solid bamboo flooring on some different types of subfloor, including underfloor radiant heat and concrete underlayment. As with hardwood floors, install a subfloor in the top of the concrete subfloor before installing the bamboo flooring. The base layer will help keep the bamboo floor warm, with a kind of cushion.
Once you have the drywall and installing new windows in your remodeled basement, you will need to decide what to do with the flooring. You may have the bamboo floor up in your home, but wonder if it can be installed in the basement. Do not worry- bamboo flooring has a low moisture absorption rate and offers an easy installation, making it an ideal choice for your basement.


Bamboo flooring options


Buy hand-scraped bamboo floor for a distressed, textured look. A little more expensive than other varieties, this soil enjoys popularity in the Middle East and Italy.


Use solid bamboo flooring or woven strand for a heavier choice ideal for a basement you plan to use as a playroom, children‘s playroom or a place for your pets. This type of bamboo flooring has a durable laminate finish. The solid bamboo floor will not expand and contract; but also offers heat resistance, so you can place it on radiant heating systems if your basement has one.


For strength materials that give the moisture a slow expansion/contraction speed, consider the bamboo engineering floor, which consists of bamboo attached to a plywood base.


Bamboo flooring Finished


Bamboo floor finishes are natural, charred and stained. For a basement with little or no natural light, consider a natural finish, which has a bright shade. A carbonized finish has a darker appearance, and each iron may appear slightly lighter or darker than the other. To match the furniture present in your basement, try a stained bamboo floor- a "particular order," and therefore more expensive, flooring.

item.title: Bamboo Flooring For Your House And Indoors
item.source: Bamboo Flooring For Your House And Indoors
item.description:
Bamboo constructions are not widely used in India. On the other hand, we use a lot of bamboo for our interior, in particular for the floor. Because in addition to its lovely aesthetic appearance, the bamboo flooring is very easy to maintain. It is virtually insensitive to moisture and temperature variations, making it a suitable material for bathrooms or heating/cooling floors for a hundred years. It is, therefore, very durable, and a sanding stroke will give it all its brilliance, in case of impact.


For its manufacture, bamboo flooring may be either solid or laminated. The solid parquet will consist of 100% bamboo stalks while the laminate is composed of a layer of 2.5mm thick on a support of compressed wood fibers or crossed layers of wood.


The solid bamboo flooring is more expensive but more resistant, and you can choose the orientation of the fibers:


Horizontal bamboo parquet with several layers (usually alternating three layers). It is the oldest technique, and it reveals the nodes in the stems.


Vertical bamboo parquet with a single layer of stems leaving the finest ribs apparent.


The densified or compressed bamboo flooring alternates the direction of the stems and allows a smoother appearance of the floor.


Regarding its implementation, it is always floating parquet to be pasted or to be clipped. Its woody structure which offers its incredible resistance, also prevents the nailing, at the risk of hurting itself.


Bamboo flooring is highly resistant ecological flooring. Thanks to its properties and its resistance to moisture, this material is an interesting choice for the floor covering of a bathroom.


Virtues of bamboo flooring as compared to hardwood ones:


Compared to hardwood floors, bamboo floors have many virtues.


The solid bamboo flooring have greater hardness, making it more durable than hardwood flooring.
The third, bamboo floors can be installed in very short time being this very conveniently, (as it came ready and finished there is no need to polish, sanding and give additional finishes like woods, which take up a lot of time to months for your Installation). Apart from the above, bamboo floors have better grain and is more elegant and graceful than hardwood flooring.


What kind of finish does bamboo flooring use and what are its strengths?


Bamboo floors are finished with seven layers of 100% solid cured, UV urethane, which makes floors abrasion resistant, chemical, and staining, fire, bleeding and oiled. Also, bamboo floors with these types of individual finishes have another great virtue in electrostatic prevention.


Why do bamboo floors become more and more familiar?


Bamboo floors are made from renewable and recyclable natural resources. Buildings, barns, boats and other structures made of bamboo often find a second life on bamboo floors, decorative panels for walls, openings, and ceilings, plus bamboo floors are an excellent choice for a healthy home.


Solid bamboo flooring, when compared to hardwood, is harder and requires less sanding and finishing, making it an excellent choice for high residential and commercial traffic applications. Bamboo has a long straight fiber composition, providing exceptional resistance to weight ratio and dimensional stability.


Bamboo has only straight grain and is not subject to extraction, leaving chips and problems common to cutting and often irregular grain alignment of many forests. The nodes of growth, a light color and straight grain of bamboo give its exotic aspect.


Bamboo, suitable for wet locations


Opinions are still divided on the possibility of using bamboo as a floor covering for the bathroom.


Nevertheless, the parquet from this plant which regenerates easily is ideally suited to the ambient humidity of a bathroom. The bamboo also has a low index of contraction and heat expansion. This reduced sensitivity to temperature changes makes it compatible with underfloor heating. Used as a floor covering, it can easily withstand the various attacks of insects, trampling, and abrasion.


Bathroom, what kind of bamboo flooring choose?


There are several types of bamboo flooring. Floating and laminated flooring and solid bamboo flooring. The first category is not recommended for floor covering of a bathroom. It resists wear and tear over time and can swell and deform. However, the risks for such a situation are zero for solid bamboo flooring. Their density and stability distinguish the latter compared to floating floors.


Bamboo flooring, precautions to be taken


To prevent the floor from moving over time, it is essential to perform the installation correctly. The battens must be installed using the glued laying technique, and a silicone bead must be applied on the periphery. Even if the bamboo can withstand moisture, it is recommended not to leave the carpet soaked on the parquet floor to avoid damaging it, as constant moisture considerably reduces the lifetime of this type of floor. Also, make sure that the bathroom is well ventilated before considering the installation of a bamboo floor.

item.title: What are the benefits of installing bamboo flooring?
item.source: What are the benefits of installing bamboo flooring?
item.description:
We evaluate together all the main advantages and defects of the bamboo flooring. Bamboo flooring has become popular in recent years due to the many similarities with wooden floors. The bamboo version is elegant, gives an exotic look to the environments and is relatively inexpensive, which makes it even more attractive.


Let‘s try and evaluate all the pros and cons of this type of flooring to make the right choice before installation and choose the one that best suits your lifestyle.


So what are the main reasons to install bamboo flooring?


Duration in time


The bamboo flooring just like the one in wood, can last many years. As in any field, quality is a key feature to establish durability, durability and reliability.


In particular, the non-carbonated bamboo is particularly resistant and can be compared to American oak parquet, but with more gear.


Elegance


The bamboo floor fits perfectly into linear environments, with modern aesthetics. Whoever chooses the bamboo parquet is attentive to the trends, but also demands a high quality.


Availability in many variants


One of the advantages of bamboo flooring is the wide choice available on the market because it is available in many styles and colors.


Keep in mind that dark-colored bamboo floors have often been thermally treated.


Eco-sustainability 


Bamboo by many is considered a very good alternative to traditional wood flooring thanks to its much faster growth and reproduction capacity. In fact a bamboo plant reaches full maturity between five and seven years.


Natural materials


The use of natural materials is depopulating in construction and bamboo flooring can be the icing on the cake in a project initiated by ecologically aware people.


Easy maintenance


The bamboo parquet is easily cleaned with a broom and a little neutral soap, no special treatment required. A great pro for those who do not have much time to clean up!


Possibility of finishing


Bamboo floors can become discolored or dull with time, but there is good news: they can be finished according to your needs because it comes with several layers of protection that are applied during installation.


If necessary the surface sanding by professionals can give new life to the bamboo floor.


Water resistance


Compared to traditional wood floors, bamboo is more resistant to water and damage caused by it, such as stains and deformations. More durable however does not mean that it does not suffer damage, so it is best to pay attention.


Low cost


Despite its exotic charm, bamboo parquet is usually less expensive than wooden parquet. What else could be better option than choosing a flooring that looks awesome and costs a small amount of money!


What are the limitations of bamboo flooring?



Scratch sensitivity


Bamboo compared to wooden parquet tends to scratch more easily. With an intensive use of an average family, it is impossible to maintain a smooth surface because pets, furniture, or heel shoes can damage the floor. Also beware of the sand!


As mentioned above under the heading "Possibility of finishing", however, it is easy to remedy the damage.


Damage caused by water


As mentioned in the Pro list, the bamboo floor is water resistant enough, but this does not exclude that, being a natural organic material, it does not cause damage caused by too much moisture, causing deformation, discoloration or mold.


Sensitive to moisture


In very humid environments, the parquet boards in bamboo are likely to expand beyond normal, or to shrink in too dry environments.


Risk of too soft materials


If the bamboo used was taken too early and did not have time to mature the risk is to be with a floor too soft and, consequently, not lasting.


Generally uncoated and stranded bamboo floors are not affected by this problem, while dark bamboo can represent a weaker structure.


Less versatile style


Though the bamboo flooring is unique in its kind and has a great appeal, it can be a limit in styles of homes very different from contemporary and modern. However, it is also true that most of the designers and flooring experts confirm that that the wooden bamboo decking is one of the finest form of flooring one can use in their homes.

item.title: All About Bamboo Flooring - Pros & Cons
item.source: All About Bamboo Flooring - Pros & Cons
item.description:
Bamboo is a natural material for surface covering having many properties of hardwood flooring. Bamboo is actually produced by a type of grass. Bamboo flooring has been an eye-catcher for many years from the time when it was launched. All bamboo flooring is designed i.e. the strands of grass are sliced and shredded and pressed together to build flooring boards.


Have a look at some of the bamboo flooring types:


Vertical bamboo possess a uniform and striped look


Horizontal bamboo has the "knuckles" in the grain pattern which is commonly associated with bamboo flooring.


The hardest and the most expensive type of bamboo flooring is strand woven bamboo mixed with glass fibers type.


Bamboo flooring has many positive benefits as well as some of the drawbacks and vulnerabilities.


There are both bamboo flooring pros and cons.


First, have a look at the pros of Natural bamboo flooring:


Nature-friendly: bamboo is composed of the natural vegetation. It is known that the bamboo plant is a highly renewable source that grows only in 3 to 5 years. The hardwood trees take about 20 years to grow completely and hence bamboo tree regrowth is much faster.


Easy to maintain: the bamboo flooring is relatively easy to maintain. Sweeping or vacuum cleaning regularly is just enough to get rid of the dust particles. You can also use bamboo floor cleaner to clean the bamboo flooring.


More resistant to water damage: the water resistance of the bamboo flooring is much more than normal flooring.


Be natural: it has become a new trend to use natural materials in the construction industry. People are becoming more ecologically conscious and hence they want to reflect this in their values. More focus has shifted on the natural material than on the costly man-made materials for the flooring of houses.


Durable and better: The strand woven bamboo is classified under the hardest and the most expensive bamboo flooring and hence is the most durable one and last longer than the other floorings.


Be trendy and stylish: if you want to elevate the elegance of your house then opt for Bamboo flooring. The appearance of the flooring is almost similar to hardwood but is still distinct and different. The bamboo flooring instantly boosts the quality of the rooms.


Refinish and renew: this is obvious that bamboo floor may require finishing after a certain period of time. It may get discolored, scratched or marred. But the advantage is that the surface can be refinished by applying the finished coats again to give it a fresh look. The thickness of the planks used decides how much sanding needs to be done.



The cons of bamboo flooring:


Scratches are certain: while it has been proved that bamboo is relatively easy to maintain but it is next to impossible to keep it up to the mark if it is used on the regular basis. The scratches on the bamboo floor can be caused by a wide variety of things like high heels, pet claws, and furniture legs. Sometimes, small grits and tiny particles can also cause nasty scratches on the bamboo floor.


Water can cause damage: bamboo is more resistant to water damage but it is still a natural material hence such excessive moisture can cause it to warp or will allow to mold to grow.


Humidity: the floor planks to plump if the flooring is installed in a humid air. If the area is much dry, then the plank might shrink. Hence appropriate temperature is required for avoiding cracks in the bamboo floor.


Lacks hardness: while strand woven bamboo flooring is much harder and durable but the bamboo planks which are darker in color are generally softer. This is because the carbonization process used to color the wood weakens it structurally.


Environmental concerns: although bamboo is a natural material which is highly renewable, it has some environmental concerns as well. The adhesive used while bamboo flooring can be toxic to the environment.
So, these are the bamboo flooring pros and cons. It is all the matter of choice. The ones who want to have bamboo flooring can avoid all the cons and have a completely easy to clean bamboo flooring in their house. While those who want a much better design to their house may not choose it.

item.title: How to Determine the Cost of Bamboo Flooring?
item.source: How to Determine the Cost of Bamboo Flooring?
item.description:
In addition to its superb rendering and comfort with pleasant contact in all seasons, bamboo flooring is virtually indestructible. More expensive than in other less noble species, bamboo flooring is now available in several manufactures, including solid bamboo and bamboo laminate, which is more affordable. Whether sticking, clipping or floating, bamboo flooring can easily be installed in any room, even in high traffic areas or in damp rooms.


Let‘s discover together the characteristics of different bamboo flooring, prices and suppliers of bamboo flooring.


Orientation of bamboo fibers


We distinguish, according to the orientation of the fibers:


Horizontal bamboo parquet: the bamboo stalks have been arranged in length on their widest edges, in order to naturally create the blade by compression of several layers (3 alternating layers in general) superimposed. It is the oldest and the simplest, which reveals the knots as they could be seen in nature for an authentic and natural effect.


Vertical bamboo flooring: it consists of a single layer of bamboo rods placed on their thinnest edges, to create the blade by their broad side, leaving finer and more delicate ribs to appear.


Bamboo densified flooring: an alternation of the direction of the bamboo rods before densification by compression makes it possible to obtain a smoother appearance without apparent ribs.


We distinguish, according to the orientation of the fibers:


Horizontal bamboo parquet: the bamboo stalks have been arranged in length on their widest edges, in order to naturally create the blade by compression of several layers (3 alternating layers in general) superimposed. It is the oldest (it is millennial in Asia) and the simplest, which reveals the knots as they could be seen in nature for an authentic and natural effect.


Vertical bamboo flooring: it consists of a single layer of bamboo rods placed on their thinnest edges, to create the blade by their broad side, leaving finer and more delicate ribs to appear.


Bamboo densified flooring: an alternation of the direction of the bamboo rods before densification by compression makes it possible to obtain a smoother appearance without apparent ribs.


Prices


Bamboo flooring cost can vary, of course, at different places depending on the quality and the workmanship (posing treatments and realization of different colors from light and dark natural). To get an idea, you must first calculate the square meters you need. These costs will then be added to the VAT which could, however, be partially recovered if it comes within the case law (restructurings and the like). The vertical type, however, costs a bit more than the horizontal one, but in this case, the choice finishing plays a crucial role. It is always convenient, therefore, to prefer the coverage of larger surfaces to plain layering in one room.



Other factors that affect bamboo flooring cost


1- Types of work


To get a new floor, you have two choices: refurbish your existing floor or install new materials. If you opt for a refurbishment, certain techniques can achieve very satisfactory results (pushing and refinishing of the floor, cleaning of the marble, etc.) at a lower cost.


2- Area to be covered


Renovating your floor does not necessarily mean changing all the floors in your home. You may want to change only the parquet flooring in the living room or the tiled flooring of the bathroom. This will affect the amount of materials needed and the length of time the installation takes place. Thus, the larger the area to be renovated, the more the price will increase proportionately!


3- Type of materials


Choosing your flooring is surely the most fun part of the renovation. However, it is also at this stage that your portfolio is most at risk. Indeed, there are several types of materials such as hardwood, ceramic, marble, vinyl or carpet, whose prices are very variable within each of the categories.


4- Installing the new floor


If you have some knowledge in renovation, motivation and plenty of free time, you could save yourself by posting your own floating wood flooring or ceramic flooring. However, some coatings are more complex to install. In such cases, professionals must be employed.

item.title: Tips and Tricks to Maintain Click Lock Bamboo Flooring
item.source: Tips and Tricks to Maintain Click Lock Bamboo Flooring
item.description:
Homeowners or construction experts who have had a fair share of dealing with bamboo floors would certainly agree that the first factor in governing their choice is durability. Whether climatic disruptions or severe stress, bamboo plants are known for standing erect in the toughest of situations and that naturally reflects when the flooring is made of the same. This however does not imply that the floors can be left exactly how they have been installed, for example- the click lock bamboo flooring are quite easy to put on, but requires proper maintenance. In fact, this applies for all the three variants- solid, engineered and strand-woven.


When compared to its counterparts like wood, the click lock bamboo types require less maintenance. But the question is how should you actually care? To retain the exceptional visual appearance, you can certainly invest in worthy cleaning products, but there is more to it. Here’s how:


Dust and dirt to be removed


You can use a broom made of fine fiber or even a dust mop to take off the loose dirt from the floor. In order to keep the floor free off dust, it is important you ensure it is dry at all rimes. Traffic on continued basis on dirty floors is akin to grit on sandpapers, which puts scratches on the finish of the floor.


The floor must be mopped


Make a mixture of vinegar and water in the ratio of 1:4, which will be a cleaning agent for the floor. There is no problem if you choose to use hardwood floor cleaner as long as you know the art of mopping properly. The moment your click-lock bamboo floor gets wet, clean it using a towel.


Keeping a dry cloth handy at all times


You cannot guarantee when there will be spills on the floor, so always keep a spray bottle filled with vinegar solution and wipe it up completely. At the most, you can dampen the cloth to a certain extent and then use it. But keep the click-lock area dry immediately.



Steaks must be polished off


If you keep a towel handy for your click-lock bamboo floor, the latter stays polished and also helps you detect ant mark left after using the damp mop or cloth. Avoid the use of oil-based cleaner as those can impart a cloudy and streaked appearance.


Floor should not be scratched


To ensure longevity of your floors, do not pull anything on the floors or better still, keep felt or coasters under the furniture so that the pieces will not mar the material when made to shift. If you have pets at your home, keep their nails trimmed. Also, say no to vacuums with beater bar for cleaning your precious click-lock bamboo floor.


Being wary about shoes worn


There requires no second mention that shoe marks can leave scuffs or dirt on your bamboo floors, especially the heeled ones. The best thing would be to keep runners or rags in the high-traffic zones to lend ample protection to the floor so as to prevent build up of dirt, scratches or scuff marks. You can also keep the mats or rugs on every doorway so as to prevent dirt from entering the room. But make sure that the rugs are cleaned or shaken out on a regular basis.


Stains removal should be the first priority


To prevent any problem, get hold of a slightly damp cloth and only the appropriate cleaning solution on the floor. If you scrub or rub the floor aggressively, the finish of the click-lock material can be harmed. Stains are best to be buffed out and the finish can be reapplied.


Steps for discoloration of the bamboo floor


Bamboo floors are hardy no doubt, but sensitive too. You can hang the curtains or blinds over windows so as to keep away the sun rays, which when exposed for a prolonged period can fade the click-lock material. Window tint can also be applied to the windows for limiting the sun rays and protecting the floor in the best way possible.


Ensuring luster of the floor


And the way to doing that would be to uses a buff sander. But stay away from waxing your click-lock bamboo floor. You can also get in touch with your manufacturer to know more about care, refinishing and overall maintenance of the flooring.

item.title: Bamboo Parquet- Solid Bamboo Flooring
item.source: Bamboo Parquet- Solid Bamboo Flooring
item.description:
Bamboo parquet is probably one of the most unknown and at the same time most interesting options. It is a very solid floor, with an elegant and original aesthetic, and suitable for interior and exterior. The bamboo parquet is today very much in vogue to decorate the home. The placement of the different sheets constitutes a true art that allows obtaining a unique interior.


On the other hand, it can also give a rather modern air to the floor of the house. Just choose a sheet of different sizes. In addition, if a more contemporary interior is preferred, it is sufficient to opt for sheets with the same dimensions.


The size of the laminates of the bamboo floor also plays an important role from a technical point of view, since they allow a greater fixation, and guarantee a better stability. The beauty of the result obtained will stand out according to the natural color of the chosen bamboo, and how the finish is established.


Advantages of Bamboo Parquet


Bamboo, rather than a type of wood, is properly an herb. Since bamboo grows very easily in those places where it is endemic (it can grow one meter per day!), its felling does not involve any aggression to the environment. That is why it is said that it is an extremely ecological option.


But the advantages of bamboo parquet are not exhausted there at all. Known by the nickname of "the grass of steel", it is one of the most stable and hard materials that exist, much more than the classic soils of oak.


In addition, as we have advanced, it is a pavement suitable for indoor and outdoor use, since it is a material resistant to moisture as well as non-slip. And being waterproof parquet, it can be used without problems in places like kitchens, washrooms or bathrooms.


Types of finishes for parquet floors


The different types of finishes are ideal for solid bamboo flooring and bamboo laminated parquet floors. The thickness of the sheets, in the case of the use of solid bamboo, is decided according to the type of installation that is intended to be made. A glued placement usually requires thick sheets of about 14 mm, but can reach 22 mm.


Only sheets more than 18 mm thick can be nailed. Dimensions may vary for glued floating models. A glazed matte finish is ideal for authentic decoration. You can also choose to lubricate the bamboo. For a more artistic look, satin nitrification is best suited. It is also possible to proceed with a brilliant nitrification that allows a modern and very chic effect.



Tips for installing bamboo parquet


The solid bamboo flooring can have about 4 mm of thickness so that the parquet is of good quality. The game that combines thickness, length and placement of the blades guarantees not only an impeccable aesthetic, but also an impeccable solidity for the floor.


There is a third version of this type of parquet, which is laminated floating bamboo flooring , so named because it is placed on a laminate floor. This model offers a special result, thanks to the meticulously studied layout of the sheets.


The work is conceived first by the designers and the photographers, so that the esthetics is absolutely exclusive. Placement plays a decisive role here in the stability of the parquet.


Finally, it cannot be forgotten that through the finish the desired final appearance can be obtained. The brushed look is the most ideal for a more authentic finish, while the smooth bamboo look offers an art deco style.


Bamboo has many of the prized properties of tree wood and is not called "green gold" for nothing. A bamboo can carry more than a ton of weight and remains flexible and light. From this strength and grace, the unique beauty of the bamboo ‘as well as its unlimited applicability. Furniture, boats, musical instruments, huts and multi-storey houses are built from it, its pods are even edible.


With its characteristics, bamboo is of course also suitable for the production of parquet. Its natural radiance gives rooms a warm and elegant atmosphere. As an environmentally friendly wooden floor, bamboo parquet is a sensible alternative to parquet made of dying tropical wood.

item.title: Bamboo Flooring - Why west is embracing this natural flooring option?
item.source: Bamboo Flooring - Why west is embracing this natural flooring option?
item.description:
Parquet is an excellent choice for floor renovation in your home. Quite a new material for bamboo flooring is bamboo, and it is becoming more and more popular these days. Bamboo flooring is a beautiful, durable and environmentally friendly floor covering, and also has an acceptable price.


Tooth Extraction Procedure


You decided that there will be no tiles, linoleum, laminate or carpet on the floor of your house, but a real wooden floor. Then you need to make the right choice among the wooden floor coverings. With this, there is no need to hurry; you need to compare all the pros and cons of different materials with the beginning.


In recent years, people prefer bamboo parquet floors, rather than classical ones. Since bamboo has many advantages in appearance and operation.


There are five main reasons why you can choose your bamboo floor.


Strength


Bamboo flooring is best suited for places where there is a lot of stress. Do not scratch if there are children or animals. Also, due to its strength, falling objects and places with frequent attendance (living room or hallway) will not harm the surface of the parquet.


Heat


Because of its natural origin, bamboo flooring keeps warmth inside your home. Most hard materials for floors have a beautiful appearance, but some try to give the unusual appearance to the emergence of the floor. Here we must not forget that sex should bring a sense of comfort. Bamboo flooring will create a combination of warmth, comfort and a beautiful appearance.


Naturalness


Bamboo flooring is environmentally friendly material because it is made from grass, which quickly grows after harvesting. For the production of bamboo, parquet is not used chemical additives.


Color


Parquet from bamboo comes in two shades. The first so-called natural light, since it fits almost any interior, its sales are skyrocketing. The second one is amber. This excellent shade is obtained by the interaction of carbon and starch, which is contained in bamboo. Such a bamboo is called "charred."


Appearance


Bamboo flooring is one of the newest floor coverings that are on the market. But it is already in great demand among buyers. Bamboo flooring will certainly embellish the look of your house or office.


Parquet from bamboo is formed in such a way that it turns out very easy. This means that the installation of such flooring in the house will be a relatively simple process. Because the bamboo fiber is compressed during production, the parquet is durable and flexible. This parquet is resistant to moisture and scratches.


Different colors and texture of bamboo flooring are achieved due to varying degrees of carbonation. Carbonized bamboo flooring, in fact, is subjected to heat treatment to darken its surface and give particular strength. The longer it heats up, the darker the color will turn out and the stronger it will be. Since, in fact, bamboo is a grass, not a tree, and then when choosing bamboo floors, it is important to pay attention to the quality of the producer.



Why is bamboo flooring unique?


Bamboo flooring is unique: the parquet provides excellent sound, noise and heat insulation, regulates the microclimate of the room and successfully resists moderate mechanical influences. Parquet from a bamboo, as well as a massive bamboo board possess high durability and provide ease of stacking.


Durable and reliable bamboo flooring is made of three-layer, glued under high pressure. Parquet is covered with five layers of wear-resistant varnish. Massive parquet from bamboo has a length of 960 mm, a width of 96 mm and a thickness of 15 mm. Parquet board made of bamboo is a unique wear-resistant material. Bamboo is one of the heaviest wood materials, it is heavier than oak by 30 percent and 3 times denser than conventional wood covers. This gives the floor coverings of bamboo natural resistance to moisture, mold and exposure to insects.


Bamboo flooring does not shrink and does not swell like the rest of hard wood flooring. Bamboo floor - the choice of a person who is anxiously related to his own home.


Parquet from a bamboo is applied for creation of unique design interiors with notes of a natural beauty. Eco-friendly bamboo flooring helps to beat stylish and non-standard interiors.


The main binding of designers to the bamboo floor is a natural decorative pattern, characteristic of bamboo, which has a parquet board made of bamboo. Bamboo floors are the epitome of fashion for environmentally friendly natural materials.

item.title: Using Bamboo is A New Trend or a Crazy for Fashionable Material?
item.source: Using Bamboo is A New Trend or a Crazy for Fashionable Material?
item.description:
Recently, bamboo flooring are increasingly used for the installation of floors in rooms of various purposes. Basically, this is all due to the fact that the bamboo covering is a safe natural material, which in its basic properties is very close to wood.


Like traditional types of wooden floors, bamboo is very versatile and, in fact, does not differ much on the floor from a wooden parquet floor with a well-finished surface or from a three-layered parquet board.


There is a huge variety of solid bamboo flooring of various types and colors from different manufacturers all over the world. In the Ukrainian market, this type of sex is represented, mainly, by Chinese manufacturers.


Numerous distribution companies and dealers offer their customers the widest choice of bamboo of various sizes, colors and types of surface finish. Basically, such coatings are delivered in the form of boards with a trimmed front surface. They can be easily installed using either an adhesive or nailing method or a floating kit.


Bamboo flooring is the ideal solution for those who want to have rich and elegant wooden floors, but cannot afford it because of their high cost. Bamboo cannot be attributed to the category of wood materials. Actually, bamboo, like a plant, is characterized as a type of grass, but the floors from it have the same beauty and warmth as the wooden floors. At the same time, bamboo floors have a much longer service life and a higher resistance to moisture.


The durability of solid bamboo floors is their huge advantage over other types of flooring. Bamboo has a high resistance to abrasion and to pressing into it hard and sharp objects. With proper care, bamboo floors will serve you for a long time.


 Fashion and trends in the modern world of flooring have many directions, most of which are oriented towards the use of natural wood. Wooden floors attract many consumers with their endless charm and beauty. They are especially popular among those people who appreciate natural materials in everything, as well as those who want to avoid the appearance of allergens, usually arising from the use of carpet flooring.


Warmer and much more durable, compared to others, wooden floors are now widely used in public spaces and in residential areas. Today bamboo is an economically viable alternative on the way to achieving the kind, beauty and durability that are inherent in wooden floors.



A few recommendations on the use of bamboo floors


Depending on the design of the board, bamboo floors can be longitudinal (with a longitudinal direction of the fibers) and transverse. Floors from the longitudinal bamboo always look more elegant. Bamboo fibers on this floor are less noticeable. At the same time, the use of transverse bamboo will give your floors a characteristic rough-contrast texture of the surface saturated with fine texture details. This type of bamboo floor is more suitable for smaller rooms.


If you want to give your room elegance, it is recommended to use a carbonized longitudinal coffee bamboo with a touch of cherry or walnut.


If you prefer the natural look of the floor, you will want to use unfinished bamboo parquet, which, as a rule, has a light color and will look great in a dimly lit or small room, creating the effect of airiness, space and increasing the width of the room.


 When laying the floor of bamboo, keep in mind that the direction of the fibers in the bamboo strip is important. Make sure that to lay the floor in the room you have prepared in the required number of slats of the same type, or transverse or longitudinal. Combination of the strips of transverse and longitudinal bamboo is highly discouraged.


Try searching for a product line from a reputable manufacturer that has a solid history and offers a long-term guarantee. This is usually a sign of durability, which goes hand in hand with hardness. But make sure the company has been in business for a while, otherwise the warranty cannot say that much in the end.


Remember that the charred version is not just a colorful product. It is rich, dark colored as a result of the production stage, which consists of boiling the strips. This is why it gives a sweeter end result.

item.title: Key Advantages of Having Bamboo Decking at Your Home or Office
item.source: Key Advantages of Having Bamboo Decking at Your Home or Office
item.description:
When it comes to the materials of building anoutdoor deck, Bamboo is often underestimated and overlooked. But we should remember that bamboo is one of the most efficient materials when it comes to the constructing. Therefore, if you are able to get good quality of bamboos then it can be very advantageous for you. Good quality bamboos can last for around 20 years which is sufficient.  Bamboo is a natural product and it has been used as a material for shelter for thousands of years. Still, in the 21stcentury, the importance of bamboo is not lost. If you are looking to build a deck with bamboo and looking for a guide then the following discussion can be handy for you. The following discussion includes all the details you should know when it comes to building a decking with bamboo. 


 


1) Durability


Bamboo is such a natural gift which is there for a long period of time. For thousands of years, bamboos have helped to give us shelters and still on the present day, the importance remains the same. The main reason for the popularity of bamboos is its durability. When it comes to one of the most durable constructing materials bamboos can be surely considered as one of them. If good quality bamboo decking can be picked then it can easily last up to 20 years. Therefore, it can be figured out how much beneficial bamboos can be.


2) Decay resistance


You can use a very high-quality material in order to construct a deck. But if it is not resistant to decay, then you can easily lose all the money which was invested in it. But if you look at bamboos, at first you won’t get the impression that is resistant to decays but it is not true. Bamboos are very good when it comes to resisting decays and that is why they can last for a long amount of time.


3) Resistant to fire


Along with being resistant to decay, bamboo decking are resistant to fire as well. Resisting fire is a very good plus point and it is very hard to find such natural constructing material which is resistant to fire. Therefore, if you are worried about your location and if you are thinking that fire can damage your deck then it is always advised to use bamboos as the constructing material.


4) Highly Stable


When you are constructing something, generally you do expect that construction to be stable. If the construction is not stable then it can be a big reason for you. At the same time, less stabilization can put a question mark on your life and your financial investments as well. If you want to get rid of all these complications, then you can definitely use bamboos as a constructing material. When you use bamboo decking, generally the construction becomes a lot stable and there is less amount of risk as well. And it is always a desirable condition for anybody.


5) Maintenance


After you have constructed a deck, the next thing you should be concerned about is the maintenance. If such materials are used which requires high maintenance then the situation may not be desirable for you. Just because when it comes to maintenance, most of the times, it can cause a hefty strike on your pocket which may leave you in a financial crisis. But if you use bamboos instead of other materials, then there is less concern over maintenance. Generally, bamboo decking does not require high maintenance and when the maintenance is required it won’t cost you a huge strike on your pocket.


6) Cost


Cost is another thing that you should consider before building a deck. You definitely don’t want to use such materials which are high in cost and at the same time requires high maintenance as well. If you are worried about cost then bamboos can be ideal for you. Generally, bamboos are very much affordable, you can get high-quality bamboos at a very good price and at the same time construction with bamboos requires less attention as well when it is about the maintenance. Therefore, if you are reluctant to use too much money for your deck construction then bamboos can be anideal product for you.

item.title: The Wonder Called Click Lock Bamboo Flooring
item.source: The Wonder Called Click Lock Bamboo Flooring
item.description:
Ever dreamed of a nice cozy house with just the perfect interior design? Well the floor of the house has been a fascination among homeowners for ages. From marble to hardwood and now bamboo we have a strange fascination for exquisite flooring. Bamboo flooring in recent years have taken over form hardwoods as the go to material for building purposes and home improvement. For centuries bamboo has been used to make houses, scaffolding and weapons by the people of Asia. However, the western world has only recently come around to the wonderful qualities that bamboo has to offer. Hardwood flooring is in the decline while demand for bamboo flooring is gradually rising. The bamboo, a tall perennial grass, is supposedly stronger than regularly available hardwoods. It is also less harmful and more beneficial to the environment.


Bamboo flooring is in trend now for quite a few years and it is here to stay. However the clever click lock bamboo flooring is creating quite the buzz among homeowners and architects alike. The click lock mechanism ensures that the bamboo planks fit perfectly and you can install your floor on your own. This type of floor does not need to be glued or nailed down, instead it sits as a floating floor which can be uninstalled and re-installed just as easily if you were to move to a new home. Such versatility of the click lock bamboo flooring is what makes it the perfect choice for your new home.


In spite of being a grass, the bamboo is one tough cookie. It can withstand an incredible 3000 pounds of force according to the Janka hardness scale, which makes it one of the hardest natural materials. It is a proven fact that bamboo is harder than most maple, oak, cherry, chestnut, walnut, ebony and mahogany. Only a few Brazilian hardwoods and an Australian buloke tree are harder than bamboo. That is quite a feat for a modest grass. Bamboo flooring is also well known for being resistant to moisture and insects. Any water spill if left untreated will eventually evaporate with time and your bamboo floor will eventually dry itself off. However be careful not to let water accumulate on your floor for more than 24 hours at a stretch. Apart from that bamboo flooring is pretty resilient and inhibits the growth of moulds, bacteria or parasites. These qualities of the bamboo prevent your floor from rotting or wearing out too early. Click lock bamboo flooring can hold out against a heavy beating and is impervious to scratches and dents. Scratches and dents if any are normally restricted to the upper layer of finishing and can be repaired by refinishing the bamboo floor. The actual bamboo underneath is sturdy and will be just fine. Refinishing can be done 2 or 3 times. Refinishing enhances the already long lasting life of the bamboo floor and makes it look like new.



Stained bamboo flooring offers a whole range of color choices to suite your style. You can settle for a rich coffee tone that lends your room a sophisticated touch or you can choose the more subtle tones for an elegant look. Whatever colors you might prefer bamboo flooring is sure to give your home a contemporary feel and a touch of smart sophistication it has been missing. The natural lines and characters of the bamboo wonderfully contrast the different shades of stains and help to provide a rustic natural feel. The click lock bamboo flooring thus adds a stylish element to your home all the while maintaining its natural appeal. The minimalistic beauty of the bamboo turns our room into a wonder retreat where you can relax after a long hard day at the office.


The cost of bamboo flooring is another blessing for any homeowner. Bamboo flooring costs around $2-$5 per square feet making it way cheaper than hardwood flooring. The easy installation of the floating floor means you also cut down on the totally unnecessary installation charges. The easy mechanism of the click lock bamboo flooring helps you to do it all by yourself. Maintaining your bamboo floor is a piece of cake as only wiping it down with a clean wet cloth twice a month will do the trick.

item.title: Why Stained Bamboo Flooring is The Way Forward
item.source: Why Stained Bamboo Flooring is The Way Forward
item.description:
While building a new house or refurnishing an old one, the one thing most people tends to overlook is the flooring. Interestingly the floor of a house gives away a lot about the home and its owners. A clean and elegant floor is something every homeowner prides themselves on and strives for. For years hardwoods has been the popular choice and go to material for building constructions. Owing to their immense strength and variety of colors and styles, hardwoods have been extensively used to build low cost houses, false ceilings and floors apart from other purposes. Such extensive use of hardwood has resulted in the depletion of the rainforests in South America which is a major ecological concern as hardwoods take almost 30-80 years to mature, sometimes even more. Cutting down of such old trees has proven detrimental to the environment and architects are now looking for an alternative to hardwood in stained bamboo flooring.


The plant in question is a tall perennial grass that grows naturally in large parts of Asia, Africa and South America. The modest grass grows throughout the year, matures in 5 to 7 years and is one of the toughest natural materials. The short generation cycle of the bamboo makes it the most sustainable building material. Bamboo is not just panda food anymore. It has found widespread use in flooring and construction material over the past few decades because of its sustainability and extraordinary hardness. Even though the bamboo has been widely used in China for centuries to build houses, scaffolding, furniture and even weapons, it came to the fore internationally in the last couple of decades. With people becoming more and more environmentally conscious, hardwoods are being gradually replaced by bamboo. 



   

So what makes such a simple grass so exceptionally popular among architects and engineers? Well first of all bamboo is stronger than maple, chestnut, oak, ash, mahogany and most walnut. This means bamboo is harder than the average hardwoods available in the market. The Janka hardness scale rates the bamboo as one of the hardest natural materials just behind Brazilian walnuts and Australian buloke. Bamboo incredibly scored nearly 3000lbf on the scale which is pretty higher than commonly available hardwoods. The robust nature of the bamboo plant also makes it resistant to dust, pests and insects. During manufacturing the bamboo is treated in a solution of boric acid and water to eliminate any insects or sugar in the bamboo shoots. This process further ensures that the bamboo inhibits future mould growth or insect infestation. Stained bamboo flooring has a reputation for being able to hold its ground against all kinds of scratches, dents and stains. Stains can be easily cleaned with the help of a clean wet cloth. Scratches are rare and even if it occurs it is mostly on the upper surface and not the surface of the bamboo. Retouching your bamboo floor is one way to get rid of scratches and keep your floor looking as good as new. Bamboo is also impervious to moisture but too much exposure to moisture for a long period of time can damage the bamboo or any other natural material for that matter. However, the naturally hardy bamboo means your floor can take a beating and still look stunning.
 

This is another great quality of bamboo floors. Stained bamboo flooring offers the same aesthetic appeal as any hardwood floor. Do not let this unassuming plant fool you. The feel of bamboo beneath your feet is great and it provides ample warmth to your room. The natural grainy texture of the bamboo lends your floor a trendy and artistic touch. With an array of stains and diverse styles on offer, stained bamboo flooring offers a luxurious experience at half the cost of any decent hardwood.
 

Yes, generally bamboo flooring costs way less than hardwood flooring. On top of that it is much easier to install a bamboo floor than hardwood floor. Bamboo floor can be nailed or glued down like hardwood or it can be set down on foam as a floating floor. You can even do it yourself. The bamboo fits perfectly ensuring minimal wastage and easy fitting. Not only does it make installing your floor easier but also makes removing the same floors a lot painless.


So the bamboo is stronger than hardwood, last longer than hardwood and is eco-friendly in nature unlike hardwood. All these make bamboo flooring the best alternative to hardwood.

item.title: Beat the Heat With the Elegant Bamboo Decking
item.source: Beat the Heat With the Elegant Bamboo Decking
item.description:
Summer is here and what better way to relax and keep cool than by splashing into your pool backward. Now for those of you who don’t have a pool then it is high time you got one. And what good is a pool if you don’t have a nice wooden deck to recline or jump into the pool from. Whenever any homeowner thinks of a deck, they go for hardwood. Hardwoods are the most popular materials when it comes to building deck. Having said so, over the past couple of decades a grass has been taking over the construction industry from hardwoods and has become the new darling in the eyes of architects and construction engineers. This grass is none other than the bamboo.


The bamboo is a very tall grass which grows predominantly throughout Asia and some parts of Africa and South America. The tall perennial grass has hollow shoots and are said to be stronger than oak or maple. It takes a bamboo roughly 5-8 years to fully mature. The generation cycle of bamboo is much less compared to hardwoods. Most hardwoods take more than 30 years to grow, while some may even take a century. Thus, cutting down of old hardwood trees for building purposes have proven fatal for the environment and the ecology. These trees take so much time to grow back that the damage caused by cutting down even one tree is irreversible. This is where the bamboo come in. with its short generation period and its incredible strength, the bamboo is a much better choice for building material compared to hardwoods, primarily because of its sustainability.


Bamboo decking also look as good as hardwood decks, if not better. The natural grains and lines of the bamboo give it an edgy texture which looks great on your deck. The artistic lines if used cleverly can make your deck look a lot more appealing than any hardwood deck. Bamboo decking also provides a diverse range of color schemes along with a variety of styles. The fact that bamboo looks exactly like hardwood will stump your neighbors and friends. What’s more, bamboo decking costs way less than hardwood decking. Using bamboo on your deck and floors will ensure less pressure on your bank accounts.



  

Bamboo has a reputation of being very low maintenance which further lowers your expenditure. Maintenance of hardwood decks are costly and is required to be done periodically. On the other hand bamboo is very easily maintained. Just a wipe with a clean wet cloth does the trick. Installing a bamboo deck is also easy as pie. You can do it yourself. Perfect fit between joists ensures there is almost no wastage of extra bamboo. The longevity of bamboo is much more than any hardwood. In fact some manufacturers even claim that a bamboo deck can last you a lifetime with refurnishing. Bamboo decking can be refurnished 2-3 times. Once refurnished, the deck will look as good as new.


Another valuable quality of bamboo is its natural ability to resist dust, pest infestation, germs and scratches. During the manufacturing process, bamboo is treated in a hot solution of boric acid. This treatment removes any insect living in the bamboo and also the stored sugar in the bamboo. By removing the sugar, the process make sure there is no future pest or insect infestation. The tough, sturdy body of the bamboo is also resilient to dents and scratches. It can also withstand the heaviest of footfalls with the minimum of fuss. Generally your bamboo decking should last a good 20 years or so but any dents or scratches can be taken care of by refurnishing the deck. After refurnishing, bamboo decking can ideally last a lifetime.


Bamboo decks are also relatively safer for your kids as bamboo tends to resist moisture and are less slippery than hardwood. However, water should not be left to accumulate at a particular spot on your deck for over 24 hours. Apart from flooding, your bamboo deck is tough enough to handle a few spills and stains. The sustainability of bamboo is what makes it a better choice amongst architects and builders. With more strength than most commonly available hardwoods like maple, oak, cherry and mahogany and greater benefits to the environment it is a perfect replacement to hardwood. Its eco-friendly values also make it attractive among homeowners who now want their homes to reflect a greener side of them.

item.title: Bamboo Plywood and its Advantages
item.source: Bamboo Plywood and its Advantages
item.description:
For years hardwood have been the go to material for plywood and furniture but over the past few decades there has been a gradual rise in the demand for bamboo plywood. Designers and architects are now looking to bamboo as a greener alternative to hardwood. Firstly bamboo is not a tree. Bamboos are very tall perennial grass as hard as some maple and oak trees. Bamboo plywood is made by cutting horizontal or vertical bamboo strips and gluing them together under high pressure to form even stronger plywood. So what makes bamboo the popular choice nowadays? Read on.


It looks like hardwood.


Don’t be mistaken. Bamboo plywood looks no different than hardwood. They have a unique texture that lends a simple yet classy look to your furniture. The natural feel of the bamboo lends a traditional touch to your home all the while keeping it contemporary with various design styles and colors. Bamboo plywood comes in two distinct styles, namely horizontal and vertical. The horizontal arrangement shows fewer lines but more character while the vertical styled plywood shows more lines but lesser natural features.


Harder than most hardwood.


Yes, you read that right. Bamboo plywood is harder than the average maple or oak plywood in the market. The greater density of the bamboo provides immense strength to the ply. Strand woven bamboo, which are made by fusing adhesive and strips of bamboo under high pressure, have been proven to be stronger than oak, ebony, maple and even most Brazilian hardwood. It has a very high score upwards of 3000 on the Janka hardness scale making it one of the hardest plywood. In fact bamboo has been in use in Asia for over thousands of years. The people of China (the highest producer of bamboo) have been using it to make houses, instruments, weapons and scaffolding.


Longevity


Bamboo plywood tends to have a longer life span than traditional hardwood. Bamboo is one of the most naturally durable materials out there. After proper treatment it resists dust and insects. They are also moisture resistant and immune to dents and scratches. Bamboo is also resistant to warping over time and can typically last a lifetime. They can easily last from 10 to 15 years with minimal maintenance. On top of that bamboo can be easily refinished 2-3 times thus increasing its lifespan. Practically they can last a lifetime.



It’s cheap and easy to install


Not only is bamboo harder than most hardwood but also cheaper than them. Since bamboo is a grass which grows in numbers and have a short harvesting cycle, bamboo is one of the cheapest materials in today’s market. It is very easy to install too. Bamboo is very comfortable to work with if you are planning to do it yourself. Bamboo plywood fits perfectly with minimal wastage and fuss.


Versatile


Bamboo plywood is extremely versatile to work with. Be it counter tops or cabinets in your kitchen or even the flooring of your home it goes just about anywhere and with anything. You can use bamboo to make furniture in your home. It might be grass but it is stronger than most hardwood and also more resilient to water and insects. The unique texture lends your furniture a touch of sophistication all the while being natural.


Easy to maintain


Cleaning your bamboo furniture is no herculean task. During the manufacturing process bamboo is boiled in a solution of boric acid to remove the sugar and any insects present. This ensures that there is no insect infestation in the bamboo even after years of use. Bamboo plywood is immune to water spills and also dust resistant. Just using a clean mop to wipe the furniture from time to time will keep it looking as good as new. Even if there is a scratch or dent you can always refinish your bamboo product easily.


Eco-friendly


Bamboos have a short life cycle of 5-7 years. This means that when a bamboo is cut down another one grows in just about 5 years time. In contrast most hardwoods take something from 30-100 years to mature and cutting down such trees cause massive environmental damages. Bamboo is thus a sustainable alternative to hardwood. Home owners nowadays want their homes and interior décor to be eco-friendly. Bamboo is the most eco-friendly building material.

item.title: All that you need to know about Click-Lock Bamboo Flooring
item.source: All that you need to know about Click-Lock Bamboo Flooring
item.description:
Bamboo being a renewable resource is quite an ideal choice for flooring. Apart from the beauty, the environment-friendliness lends the material an upper hand when compared to its counterparts like wood. It is for this reason that homeowners and construction contractors are happy while using it for flooring requirements.


Types of Bamboo Floors


If you are looking forward to installing bamboo floors at your place, it makes complete sense to know the various types of bamboo floors.


The first is the solid one, which is available of varying lengths and is attached together with the use of nails or adhesive.


The second type is the engineered one that looks similar to the laminate flowing and can also float on the surface of other flooring. Now this type can be installed via a method called click and lock. The best part about this type of bamboo flooring is that no nails or adhesives are required to ensure that the floor is in place.


The third, often regarded as the best form is a little expensive because of the bamboo strands being woven together that offer it a high level of durability.


Factors to consider while making a choice


Prior to selecting the type, it makes sense to understand what the age of the bamboo is. Ideally, any high-quality bamboo flooring is made from bamboo cane that should not be less than 4 years. In order to mature, any bamboo plant requires a minimum of 4 to 5 years.


Besides, you should also check for the finish of the material. If the final lacquer finish of the bamboo flowing is good, then the lasting will also be great.


The Click-Lock Type


Talking about the click lock system in bamboo flooring, this kind usually snaps together or ‘clicks’ together to look exactly like tongue-and-groove flooring. The click lock or snap lock or simply snap together bamboo flooring (whatever you would like to call it) is fit as a DIY work. No extra tools are required and you don’t even have to clean-up or wait for the glue to dry. Simply install it at once and then use it within some time.



In contrast to other engineered floors, the click lock bamboo can be refinished 2-3 times. The former usually has a thin veneer of wood on top. But with click-lock floors, the durability is great and a re-sandable 1/8 inch thick wear layer of strand bamboo can be added to provide high dimensional stability. The floors are also humidity-friendly and are perfect for use in beaches, lakes, riverfront homes and so on.


One thing to keep in mind is that the click lock bamboo flooring are easy to take apart as they are when put together. Once you ‘unclick’ the boards, the job is done. So you need toe nsure few thinsg beforehand when choosing a bamboo flooring with locking or snapping together system.


Firstly, check to see that the product adjusts to the humidity of the room. Keep it for 72 hours before you begin the work. Imagine a dry winter day when your home’s heating system is kept on and the bamboo flooring is likely to shrink if the relative humidity drops below 40%.


Secondly, the sub-floor to be installed on should also be clean, dry, level and structurally fine. If you have to install on a concrete sub-floor, it is recommended to use a moisture barrier. Read the manual or check the website to follow the instructions. It is amazing but sometimes the most inexperienced homeowner can install the engineered click lock floors.
If you have a solid click-lock bamboo floor, there are a number of advantages. It’s easy to install and can be refinished up to 5 times. But on the flip side, the suitability is only meant for humidity conditions owing to increased shrinkage effect and that is exactly when humidity levels decrease by 15-20%.


On the other hand, engineered click-lock bamboo floor has very high dimensional stability. However, it can be refinished only 2 times and the maximum recommended runs only when the interior humidity will vary above 15% throughout the year.


Pay close attention to the type of flooring you require and only then select this one.
