Although there is considerable difference between the traditional and modern approach of bamboo flooring, latest technology and processes have made bamboo even sturdier, durable and stronger.


Types of Bamboo Floorings Available in Market


Engineered Bamboo Flooring: You might have heard or seen horizontal grain or horizontal cut bamboo floors, which is nothing but engineered bamboo flooring. Here flat bamboo strips with solid layer are glued to another substrate. Offering the most elegant and easiest way of installing, engineered bamboo floor offers the most elegant and distinctive horizontal ring markings on the finished floors.


Solid Bamboo Flooring: By gluing, together solid bamboo pieces solid bamboo flooring which sometimes is also called as vertical cut or vertical grain bamboo flooring you get this beautifully finished flooring planks. Usually solid bamboo is considered as stringer and more sturdier than engineered counterpart of bamboo flooring is. After installation, it offers thin strip look as the bamboo strips are compressed together in vertical fashion.


Strand Woven Bamboo Flooring: In this type, bamboo is shredded rather than cutting and mixing suitable adhesives to make it harder and stronger; it is then compressed to make harder bamboo planks. Probably this type of flooring is strongest and hardest than above two types. More often stranded woven flooring does not have natural or traditional bamboo aura. However, the entire manufacturing process offers enough flexibility to the manufacturers in creating versatile length, patterns, textures, styles and colors in bamboo floorings.

item.title: Want to Buy Bamboo Floors?
item.source: Want to Buy Bamboo Floors?
item.description:
When there are so many options and varieties of flooring are available in market then why increasing number of consumers are interested to install bamboo floor. Well, due to the increased durability, cost effectiveness, toughness, hardness and water resistant quality undoubtedly bamboo is one of the most pursued flooring materials these days.


Bamboo Floors Offer Style Strength and Comfort


Being environmentally responsible more and more homeowners are inclined towards using bamboo as first choice for flooring material. Due to the rising awareness of preserving environment and natural habitats bamboo is considered as the safest and environment conserving material that can be used for flooring rather than hardwood. Bamboo not only is considered as safe and environment friendly but also is also stronger, durable and cost effective compared to other flooring options in hardwood and laminates. Furthermore, the style, elegance and aesthetically pleasing look it provides to the entire home add beauty and glamour to the entire interior decorum of homes thereby increasing its value.


Tips for Choosing Bamboo Flooring


First thing to consider before buying bamboo flooring is color. You have to be specific and should possess clear and concise idea of what type of color you need in bamboo that sill justify and suit the existing interior theme of your home. Usually there are two major options in bamboo flooring when it comes to color, natural and carbonized. If you prefer natural color then it will be little pale having natural bamboo color but if you want darker shade of color then you should settle for carbonized bamboo boards.


Additionally if you want bamboo color representing rainbow color then asking bamboo floor dealer about stained bamboo flooring is better option. Apart from the major natural and carbonized bamboo colors stained bamboo floors provides you flexibility and convenience to choose almost any color you desire.


Second thing is style, although there are different patterns and styles in bamboo floors major types are vertical and horizontal grains. These types have acquired their name due to the gluing process in which the bamboo strips are attached either in vertical or horizontal fashion. Each type has it distinctive aura and is potential enough to bring in the required warmth, beauty and elegance to your home floorings.


Recently a new pattern called engineered flooring has become increasingly popular in bamboo floors. When you have rooms with sufficient amount of moisture, then using engineered bamboo floors is the best option. Due to unmatched water resistant this type of flooring will prevent cupping, wrapping and warping of floor compared to its other counterparts.

item.title: Maintaining Bamboo Flooring
item.source: Maintaining Bamboo Flooring
item.description:
In this era of green building, bamboo flooring is a favorite among many homeowners. A versatile, durable, affordable and sustainable form of hardwood flooring, bamboo is the floor of choice for those building or renovating houses with an eco-friendly edge. Bamboo floors can be adapted to any style of decoration, offering a stunning look to any room. The material itself can be kept natural or dyed into various colors, whether finished or unfinished. Bamboo can also be found at reasonable prices, making it an ideal option when redecorating on a budget.


Bamboo has a great appearance with characteristics such as knuckles and growth rings that add texture to the floor. Once the flooring has been purchased, the pieces have to adjust to the home’s climate for several days, so the homeowner should spread them in small piles. Installation of bamboo floors is quite easy. The can be installed on top of concrete or wood and above or below grade.


If bamboo flooring installation is to be done on a cement floor, using glue is the way to go. The homeowner can work in small sections, connecting bamboo boards as he/she goes. A mallet can be used to ensure they fit tightly. Otherwise, the flooring can be held down using nails or the homeowner can create a floating floor by snapping together the strips on top of a foam layer. A horizontal cut is recommended since it offers a wider strip and also shows more bamboo markings.


Just as is the case with other hardwood floors, certain factors are important in order to keep a bamboo floor as beautiful as the day it was installed. Water should be prevented from collecting on the floor as it can lead to warping. Any spills should be cleaned up thoroughly as soon as they happen. Areas on the floor that are under a sink, water dispenser or icemaker should have a small rug for absorbing water.


As much as bamboo is easy to maintain, it can dent or scratch just like wood. The floor should be dry-dusted or swept daily, but should never be waxed. To keep the floor fresh looking, it should be swept using a soft broom and mopped with natural cleaners. Only a damp mop should be used- water or any cleaning product should never be poured directly onto the floor. It is advisable to check into a warranty as most suppliers offer structural and finished warranty. The homeowner can also a scratch and burn repair kit from the bamboo flooring manufacturer.


The layers of finish should be sufficient to protect the floor from wear and tear for a long time. If necessary, most bamboo floors can be refinished and sanded in the course of their lifetime. The homeowner should ensure that he/she places plastic protectors or soft pegs under furniture legs to prevent scratching. Placing rugs in high traffic areas like on doors is also a good idea. High-heeled shoes should be avoided on the floor. The homeowner can try to keep the claws and mails of pets trimmed to avoid scratches on the floor.

item.title: Bamboo Flooring Installation Techniques
item.source: Bamboo Flooring Installation Techniques
item.description:
Until now, you might have heard a lot about bamboo floors, its advantages, its durability, its cost effectiveness and its environment friendliness. Chances are more that you also might have heard about ease it provides in installing floor planks. The only thing you might not have heard or read is about the different types of bamboo floor installation techniques. Here we will consider few commonly used installation methods as each method has its pros and cons. Therefore having outright knowledge of bamboo floor installation you can easily decide on the best installation method that suits your budget and your requirements.


Methods Used to Install Bamboo Floor


Direct Sticking: Direct sticking is probably the most preferred and commonly used installing technique. Bamboo floor planks are directly glued to the subsurface, which offers a quite floor to walk on. In this method glue is toweled on the undersurface and bamboo planks are laid on them in specific manner which given permanent and string floor installation. If high quality adhesive is used then keeping planks in place and without producing any gaps or cups you are ready on walk on your newly installed floor in just few hours.


Floating Floor: When you want to install bamboo floor using floating floor method then it is necessary that you should prepare high density but thin underlay. Rather than gluing boards, they are attached using tongue and grove present on all sides of the boards. As the floor, usually floats from the underlying surface this method is called floating floor. Due to the structural design of bamboo planks made to suit floating floor installation method this is probably the most favored and easy installation method.


Plank on Ply: Until now much preferred for installing timber floor, this superior floor installation method can be utilized for installing sturdy and durable bamboo floors. In this technique plywood sheets usually 12 mm thick are nailed and attached to the subfloor with adhesive. Then bamboo boards then secretly nailed and glued to the ply, as it provides easy and comfortable surface for the bamboo boards for installation. Although this is rare installation method not much favored and used, regions with high moisture and homes with small undulation flooring are the preferred locations to use this floor installation method.


Acoubond: Sika International is the company behind inventing this method of installation as it prevents noise to pass one from upper to the lower floor. Usually in high-rise apartments sound absorption system is must therefore using this Acoubond installation method is compulsory in some countries. In this method foam mat is used as undersurface for bamboo floorings on which bamboo boards are laid. Having done this not only, this floor reduces and absorbs noise but it also rectifies surface irregularities in floor.

item.title: Introduction to Strand Woven Bamboo Flooring
item.source: Introduction to Strand Woven Bamboo Flooring
item.description:
What is Strand Woven Flooring?


Bamboo is highly fibrous. Regular manufacturing methods normally laminate these fibers one on top of the other, but in the strand woven method, the fibers are woven together on an adhesive base, leading to a stronger plank.


Stranded woven bamboo floors are created when Bamboo stalks normally averaging five years of age are boiled in a solution of boric acid and water to remove sugar content as an anti- termite preventive measure. They are then dried thoroughly and weaved together.


The next process in the formation of strand woven flooring is crushing the woven material under extreme heat which is then milled to create boards. Following the milling, each board is sanded down and then coated with aluminum oxide, which is considered to be an excellent flooring finish. This endows the boards to withstand any tough conditions.


Strand woven flooring is considered as an upgrade to the traditional bamboo flooring. Strand woven Bamboo flooring is also allergen free, which can come as a boon to many household nursing asthmatic patients.


Uses


Strand Woven bamboo can be used in dry areas and where moisture content or the accumulation of moisture is less. Strand woven flooring can be used in living room, hallways, and bedrooms.


Bamboo Floor Maintenance


Like most wood floors, bamboo wood flooring too should be handled carefully. One should use a dust mop to remove the dirt and grime rather than splashing water to wipe the dirt. A bristled room can be used to remove the stubborn grit and dust from the crevices.


When it is necessary to mop, ensure that there is no extra water in the mop by wringing out all the water from the mop; mop should be wet not watery


 There is an erroneous perception among the homeowners that the floor planks made of strand woven bamboo are not as hard as real woods. The janka testing proves the fact that the strand woven is as hardy as the next wooden tree.


Pros of Installing Strand Woven Bamboo Flooring


Strand woven bamboo flooring is quite budget friendly in comparison to hardwoods.


Strand woven flooring is sturdy and is pet and family friendly. They can be installed in high traffic areas without having to worry about the wear and tear. Since sugar is removed while boiling the wood with boric acid solution, the chances of termite attacking these types of woods are minimal. Strand woven bamboo flooring can give any place, be it home or office a unique, appealing look unlike other wood floorings.

item.title: Bamboo Flooring Important Features
item.source: Bamboo Flooring Important Features
item.description:
Undoubtedly, hardwood flooring is the most popular flooring trend these days amongst homeowners and property developers. After stone, vinyl and tile flooring hardwood flooring have gained its much-awaited anticipation. For improving overall value of your home, for durability, for minimum maintenance and for allergen free flooring bamboo flooring is considered best flooring options. Different people have different reasons for choosing bamboo flooring, it does not matter, what your reasons are but what matters is what you know about bamboo flooring.


Advantages of Using Bamboo Flooring


#1: Unmatched Bamboo Properties


Usually when you are installing floors for your home, no one likes floors that need replacements after few years. Bamboo for sure is the hardest hardwood floor compared to other options. Considerably the strength rating achieved by bamboo is relatively higher than maple and red oak. Therefore, bamboo flooring is expected to stand tough for any kind of wear and tear for longer duration. Being natural resilient bamboo will withstand any kind of dents of pressures preserving its durability and look. Additionally bamboo with its natural water resistant quality becomes most favored option for flooring and when it undergoes lamination process then it becomes additionally resistant to wrapping and gaping.


#2: Aesthetic Appeal of Bamboo Flooring


In no manner bamboo should be mistaken for wood as it basically is a type of grass thus bamboo usually has a very distinctive look compared to hardwood flooring obtained from trees. The natural color of bamboo with some darker tints and sometimes, lighter bands from the nodes make it even more attractive and alive. When bamboo flat boards are prepared then usually they are made in such manner that they all have uniform color and tight grain matching each other. Only if you want a dark colored bamboo floor then you can think of carbonized bamboo, which makes the bamboo color darker from within using sugar present in bamboo flanks. However if you want bamboo color to suit your interior designing theme then preferring stained bamboo floors in variety of colors will offer you the color of your choice.


#3: Bamboo Floors Offer Environmental Benefits


If you are environment conscious then bamboo floor is just for you as bamboo is a grass plant, which can be harvested again in quick time compared to trees. Bamboo needs only five years to grow up to 50 feet whereas hardwood trees require at least 30 years to grow and develop that much. Although you can plant and harvest new bamboo plants usually bamboo grows from the cut sprouts needing no additional harvesting efforts. Being natural in origin, you will require fewer chemicals and fewer efforts to maintain and clean your bamboo floors compared to other floor types.

item.title: Detailed Insight on Bamboo Flooring
item.source: Detailed Insight on Bamboo Flooring
item.description:
Gone are the days when hardwood and laminated flooring was the only flooring choice of majority of consumers. These days more and more people are interested in experiment with the newest and revolutionary flooring option ‘Bamboo Flooring’. Initially bamboo was considered as trendy and cheap flooring options. However, in past few years’ bamboo floors have proved their versatility, sustainability, durability and cost effectiveness to world. Furthermore after people got to know the environment friendly properties of bamboo people interested to go green and preserve nature could not settle for other option than bamboo floors. Even if you are planning to install bamboo flooring but want a little insight then surely this article will clear all your doubts.


What Actually Bamboo Is


In almost every corner of earth, you will find bamboo referred as kind of grass. However the best quality bamboo and one that is typically used for flooring is produced in vast majority in China, Indonesia and Vietnam. Due to the favorable conditions and healthy environment offered in these countries, bamboo grows to almost 3 feet per day in these regions. Within five to six years, bamboo grows to their optimum height and potential ready to be converted in to planks. The best thing is bamboo usually harvests from the cut sprouts without need of replanting. With hardness, rating almost 25 times greater than red oak and little higher than maple wood bamboo is considered as safest, toughest and cheapest flooring alternatives to hardwood and laminates.


What Options You Have in Bamboo Flooring

 
Usually there are three major options in bamboo flooring horizontal and vertical grain as well strand woven. Each of this option has its unique and distinguished look with differentiating performance.


Horizontal grain bamboo floors are prepared by lying splits in horizontal position and then stacking them three high to be glued together. The finished bamboo plank is so attractive that you can actually see bamboo knuckles giving then the appearance of bamboo stalks.


Bamboo planks with vertical grains are made by laying bamboo splits in vertical position and afterwards gluing them together. In this kind of bamboo planks, bamboo knuckles are usually hidden but you get an outstanding appearance of long but narrow natural bamboo strips.


Stranded woven bamboo planks are made by mixing different bamboo scraps together using and then compressing them to produce finished bamboo planks. Usually in this type, the appearance of bamboo planks is random and occasionally bamboo knuckles are visible.

item.title: Pros and Cons of Bamboo Floors
item.source: Pros and Cons of Bamboo Floors
item.description:
Until now, you might have heard of using hardwood, stones or laminates for flooring; but have you heard of using grass for flooring. Surprised, you should be; because, these days use of grass for flooring is one of the latest trends making buzz in interior decoration industry. Well, you guessed it right we are speaking about bamboo flooring.


Things You Need to Know About Bamboo


Having tree like structure and growing in shrubby form with hollow woody stems, bamboo is one of the most ancient building materials used by our ancestors. Although bamboo is hollow from inside, it gathers its strength from this same structure as it has rigid and sturdier internodes. Within six to seven years, matured bamboo trunks are utilized for manufacturing highly durable, aesthetically pleasing and long lasting bamboo floor planks. The best thing about bamboo is you need not have to replant the grass as it regrows from the remnants of the rhizomes from cut bamboo. Not only bamboo is fast growing natural flooring product but it also takes less space for harvesting compared to that is needed by other hardwood options. Initially it is hard to think or consider bamboo as flooring material but after processing and compressing techniques bamboo becomes hardest and sustainable flooring material.


Pros of Using Bamboo Flooring


Bamboo is supposed to have developed natural moisture and fire resistance and have natural insect repelling abilities.


As bamboo is no place where dust, dander and mildew is harbored it provides completely allergen free home environment keeping every family member safe and healthy.


With staining technique, it is possible to get bamboo flooring matching the overall or existing interior decorum of home.


Bamboo floor planks are available in wide variety of styles, patterns, textures and colors so choosing the most suitable flooring are always possible. Additionally the ease it provides in installation is simply unmatched to other options present in flooring.


Harder than red oak and maple wood, bamboo is also durable and renewable which makes it first choice for environment concerned people.


Being easy top clean and maintain, look, feel and texture of bamboo flooring can be preserved for years.


Cons of Bamboo Flooring


Bamboo has a hard surface therefore rather than absorbing sound, it reflects it making them noisier.


If exposed to direct sunlight, bamboo with its natural property to bleach changes its color from original or stained color that might deteriorate your purpose of installing bamboo floorings.


Lastly, bamboo has been in market for a short while so its long-term implications, effects and durability is still not known properly. Therefore, it is hard to pass any judgment on wear and tear of bamboo flooring in long run.

item.title: Bamboo Flooring Reviews
item.source: Bamboo Flooring Reviews
item.description:
Bamboo is a natural surface covering grass displaying the properties of hard woods like Oak and birch. Bamboo is a natural, renewable source, ready for use within three to four years of planting unlike the trees which take up to twenty years.


Bamboo flooring sellers and manufacturers advocate the usage of bamboo citing its tensile power and its resistance to insect attacks. Bamboo is quickly becoming the flooring of choice among the urban crowd while bamboo has always been the choice of rural lot because of its easy availability.


Bamboo is a stylish flooring surface which can elevate the effect of the room almost instantly. Bamboo itself can be dyed in any color one fancies or kept completely natural.


Coloring of Bamboo


Once the bamboos are cut into strip, the manufacturers have the option of keeping the strips normal, or deepen the color by carbonizing it or stain the boards into desired colors.


Natural bamboo: After the cutting and stripping of the bamboo tree, the strips are boiled in hot water to remove impurities. The hot water bleaches the color of Bamboo to blond. Blond is said to be the natural color of bamboo. If the owner or the manufacturer decide to keep the color natural, then the process ends here, and the boards are glued together to form a strong plank.


Carbonized bamboo: Immediately after stripping, the boards are subjected to high pressure steaming and carbon is introduced into the steam chamber. Carbon enters the strip and dyes the entire strip. The colors may range from caramel color to light coffee. Bear in mind, the process of carbonization decreases the strength of the boards.


Stained bamboo: bamboo planks can also be painted any colors, to match your exterior or interior. The dye is painted on the boards or rubbed on by hand.


Installing the Bamboo Floors


Before installing the bamboo floors, it is left in the room where it is to be installed for a couple of days. This is done so that the board gets used to the room temperature and does not warp or twist itself out of shape after a few days. Bamboo flooring can be installed over any type of subflooring.


Taking Care of the Floor


As with any hardwood floor, water should be kept off the floor. If there is any water spill, wipe the floor instantly.


Dry dusting on the floor is enough to clean the surface, but that does not mean that you cannot indulge in thorough cleaning. Once in a while, when thorough cleaning is needed, run a dry mop over the floor. When you have to place heavy objects on the surface of the floor, pad the area with heavy felt piece of cloth or padding.

item.title: Bamboo Flooring Innovates Design World
item.source: Bamboo Flooring Innovates Design World
item.description:
Are you in search for different things needed in your home? Well, you need to have unique idea and this means avoiding the materials your neighbors may have already used especially when it comes to your flooring. A more natural look would be good for your flooring and one of the ideas you can have is bamboo flooring. This will give a new and trendy style for your home.


 Bamboo flooring  Advantages:


There are 3 reason to why bamboo flooring is an excellent material you can use and these are:


1) The uniqueness of your flooring

2) The natural look of your flooring

3) The environmental benefits


Excellent Qualities of Bamboo


Selecting flooring for your house means you only want it to last for a long time. You don’t want flimsy flooring that would cost you more because you need to replace it again after a few years. Well, bamboo is a strong material and you can even compare it with other wood type floorings that are made from hard wood such as oak or walnut. The seller and manufacturer of bamboo flooring is quite important, too. Great quality is the first choice than the cheap price.


Since bamboo is really sturdy, it can last for a long time  and can survive from the elements. As a result, your flooring would last for a longer time and you don’t have to spend more when it comes to renovating your flooring.


One of the factors to why bamboo flooring is sturdy is that it’s water resistant. Remember, bamboo when dried well can resist water and thus making the material last longer.


As a matter of fact, because bamboo flooring is water resistant, it has been used even in kitchen renovations where other types of hardwood flooring materials are not advisable for use as flooring.


The Aesthetic Worth Of Bamboo

Well, you might be thinking that bamboo can’t be complemented on your flooring because the color is light, it can still be done if you want it dark. Remember, bamboo is versatile and you can do just about anything to it.


Final Thoughts


If you are in search for a flooring idea and in a way unique, you can always opt for bamboo material for your flooring. It’s sturdy and will surely last longer without having too much expenses.

item.title: Bamboo Flooring Gaining popularity
item.source: Bamboo Flooring Gaining popularity
item.description:

item.title: Solid Bamboo Flooring Review
item.source: Solid Bamboo Flooring Review
item.description:
Bamboo is a large tubular grass with a hard outer shell, making it suitable to use as an alternative for woods, thereby saving many forest lands from destruction. Bamboo is extensively used as flooring material in many East Asian countries.


Bamboo flooring sales have shot up over the years and the reasons are quite obvious; they are attractive, versatile, affordable and above all environment friendly.


Basic Forms of Flooring


Bamboo flooring comes in two basic forms: solid planks and engineered planks.


Solid, tongue and groove bamboo is handled and installed similar to the other regular hardwood flooring. The planks are secured down with nails or staples with or without mastic.  As we all know, nailing  and stapling can be a time consuming process, So is the installation of solid flooring normally takes twice as long as engineered planks to install.


The good news is, solid bamboo flooring  produces a permanent and rock solid floor; they also come prefinished and one can transport all your things  as soon as you finish flooring instead of having to wait until the finishing’s polish dries.


There are three different kinds of solid bamboo flooring:


1) Vertical grain solid strip
2) Flat grain solid strip
3) Strand bamboo


Vertical grain solid strip is composed of thin bamboo strips stacked on the edges and glued together. These floors give a mottled look and are ideal for hiding dirt as well as providing an interesting look to the room


Flat grain is the most common method of preparing Solid wood. In this process, the thin, flat strips of bamboo are stacked one atop the other and then laminated together.


Strand bamboo is obtained from super thin   shredded bamboo fibers that are mixed together with resins and pressed into rock hard planks.

Costs


A solid bamboo plank costs less than engineered planks. Prices are often based on the thickness of the planks; thicker the plank, greater will be the price.


Warranties are excellent indicators of the quality of wood. The best wood comes with a longer warranty as compared to low cost wood.


Advantages of Solid Bamboo


Solid bamboo finish gives one the most natural look amongst other types of bamboo flooring. The surface of the board will have quite rich features and some interesting patterns enhancing the ‘look’ of the room to another level.


Scratches and dents tend to occur on the woods after some time on the floors. With solid bamboo planks, one can sand down and refinish the surface at frequent intervals, making it look new and shiny again.

item.title: Using Bamboo Flooring for Houses and Businesses
item.source: Using Bamboo Flooring for Houses and Businesses
item.description:
There is a global acceptance for bamboo-based products due to its nature-friendliness as well as other functional features in terms of beauty and endurance. Bamboo floors are lately coming up as a trend in almost all the countries and it surely has got many advantages when compared to the traditional flooring types.


Bamboo is a very flexible and friendly material, which can be easily replenished and it is also cheap when compared to many other materials used for flooring and supply is also there in plenty. The installation and maintenance of bamboo flooring is also pretty easy. Further we will discuss about some unique benefits of using bamboo flooring for your home or business space.


Its eco-friendly


The major reason why people are getting attracted towards bamboo is that it is nature-friendly. The growth of the bamboo plant is much quicker than many other woods used to lay on the floor. Not just for flooring, but bamboo is being used for many construction purposes in interiors and exteriors and has got long-lasting and endurable features, which make it very user-friendly too.


Highly cost effective


Compared to marbles, granite, or any other synthetic flooring tiles or materials you use, bamboo is far cost-effective than any of these. Even on considering the hardwood options for flooring, you can find bamboo as the cheapest without compromising on quality, finish, and beauty. So, for those who are planning to do cost effective flooring to your house or shops, bamboo flooring is surely a pocket-friendly option.


Highly versatile


As far as the shades and grains are considered, you can find a wide range of natural varieties to choose from in bamboo. As there are a varied selection to be made, it should not be a difficult task for you to choose an appropriate variety to match to your décor and walls. Also, as there are variety of grains available, you can bring in an intelligent mix by offering a unique look to the floors of each room to best match to the mood and purpose. Bamboo floors are also resistant to the change in temperature and season, so it can be installed at any location without worrying about the dampness or heat.

item.title: Advantages of Strand Woven Bamboo Flooring
item.source: Advantages of Strand Woven Bamboo Flooring
item.description:
The general concept about flooring whether it be the home flooring or the same for a commercial space of office set-up, it should be durable as well as tough. There are plenty of materials being used for flooring purpose, both natural as well as synthetic. Tile materials, different types of natural stones like marble and granite, as well as wood are usually being used for flooring. Lately, among all these, one very tough and durable material, which is in fact very beautiful and eco-friendly too, is strand woven bamboo flooring.


While considering it, you can see that this material is even tougher when compared to the other flooring materials and you can easily compare it with the durability of cherry, oakwood and hickory. Bamboo is rather a plant wood, which is being used for multiple purposes like making furniture, walls, blinds etc.


It is found to be highly durable, and not say, very beautiful in its looks. Strand woven bamboo flooring is becoming much popular lately as the strength it gains through the stranding process is far higher than that of the raw material.


Different species of bamboo


Bamboo is there in plenty of species. The specific species which is being used to produce the strand-bamboo floors is known as Moso. The making process include cutting bamboo in small strips and then it is boiled. The boiling will remove any of the unwanted plant substances which may probably attract the termites on a long run.


Then the strands will be dried and high pressure will be applied on to it. Along with the pressure an adhesive also will be added, which in turn gets the strand flattened and mold it into the form of planks. As the final product, we get a very dense and strong plank, which can be used for flooring. The strand woven bamboo flooring thus withstand high traffic as well as furniture and other materials. The appearance of this material is also very unique and give a truly natural feeling.


The installation of strand woven bamboo flooring is also pretty and more or less similar to other kind of general flooring installation. The planks can be applied directly on to the asphalt floor with the use of strong glue or nails. There is also the alternate option of making use of the floating type installation, in which the bamboo planks can be installed anywhere regardless the structure of the floor. It is pretty easy to maintain also.
